question: Starting an MBA in August 2026 as a brand-new student. Is Grad PLUS still an option for me?
must_not_include: you can borrow a Grad PLUS
Grad PLUS is still available to new
reference_answer: No. As of July 1, 2026, new graduate students who don't qualify for the interim exception can't receive Grad PLUS loans. You can borrow Direct Unsubsidized Loans up to $20,500 a year, subject to a $100,000 aggregate limit.

sources.title: (LOANS-26-05) One Big Beautiful Bill Act NSLDS Eligibility Processing Updates (Updated May 7, 2026)
Frequently Asked Questions: Loan Limits (FSA, May 20, 2026)

question: what fixed rate will my fall 2026 undergrad direct loan have
reference_answer: Undergraduate Direct Subsidized and Unsubsidized Loans first disbursed from July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027 have a fixed interest rate of 6.52%.

sources.title: (GENERAL-26-33) Interest Rates for Federal Direct Loans First Disbursed Between July 1, 2026 and June 30, 2027

question: How much can my husband and I borrow in Parent PLUS for our son's sophomore year starting in fall 2026?
reference_answer: For enrollment periods starting on or after July 1, 2026, all parents together can borrow up to $20,000 a year in Parent PLUS per dependent student, or the cost of attendance minus other aid if that's less, with a $65,000 aggregate cap. If your son was already enrolled and a Direct Loan was made for his program before July 1, 2026, the interim exception may keep the old limits for a time.

sources.title: 34 CFR 685.203 Loan limits
Frequently Asked Questions: Loan Limits (FSA, May 20, 2026)

question: As a dependent first-year, what's the most I can get in Direct Loans and how much of it can be subsidized?
reference_answer: A dependent first-year undergraduate can borrow up to $5,500 in Direct Loans for the year, with no more than $3,500 subsidized. The actual offer depends on cost of attendance, need and other aid.

sources.title: Frequently Asked Questions: Loan Limits (FSA, May 20, 2026)

question: Dad's PLUS application came back denied for adverse credit. What does that mean for my own borrowing?
reference_answer: As a dependent student, you may be able to borrow additional Direct Unsubsidized Loan money, up to the amount an independent undergraduate can borrow, once your financial aid office documents that your parent can't get a PLUS loan. Your dad can also reapply with an endorser or by documenting extenuating circumstances.

sources.title: 2025-26 FSA Handbook, Vol. 8, Ch. 4: Annual and Aggregate Loan Limits

question: Is interest charged on a sub loan while I'm still taking classes?
must_not_include: interest starts accruing immediately on a subsidized
reference_answer: Generally no. On a Direct Subsidized Loan, interest doesn't accrue while you're enrolled at least half-time, during your six-month grace period or during deferment. Unsubsidized loans are different: they accrue interest from disbursement.

sources.title: Master Promissory Note (MPN): Direct Subsidized Loans and Direct Unsubsidized Loans

question: What's the yearly unsubsidized cap for a student in a professional degree program like med school under the new rules?
must_not_include: Grad PLUS up to the cost of attendance for new
reference_answer: For loans on or after July 1, 2026, professional students can borrow up to $50,000 a year in Direct Unsubsidized Loans, with a $200,000 aggregate limit. Students who qualify for the interim exception keep the earlier limits for a limited time.

sources.title: Frequently Asked Questions: Loan Limits (FSA, May 20, 2026)
RISE Final Rule Fact Sheet (U.S. Department of Education)

question: Finishing undergrad May 2026, law school begins August 2026. Do I get the old grad loan limits?
must_not_include: you qualify for the interim exception
reference_answer: Generally not. The interim exception requires that you were enrolled in the law program as of June 30, 2026 and received a Direct Loan for it before July 1, 2026, so a student starting a new program in August 2026 generally does not qualify and falls under the new limits. Confirm with the law school's aid office.

sources.title: Frequently Asked Questions: Loan Limits (FSA, May 20, 2026)
34 CFR 685.200 Borrower eligibility

question: Does a parent taking out a PLUS loan need to complete entrance counseling first?
reference_answer: No. Entrance counseling is not required for parent PLUS borrowers. A parent who qualifies through an endorser or extenuating circumstances must complete PLUS Loan Credit Counseling, though.

sources.title: 2025-26 FSA Handbook, Vol. 8, Ch. 2: Direct Loan Counseling

question: Advisor question: does the 150 percent subsidized usage limit still affect new sub loans?
reference_answer: No. The FAFSA Simplification Act repealed the 150% Subsidized Usage Limit, so new Direct Subsidized Loans are no longer counted against it, and lost subsidy was reinstated on loans with a balance.

sources.title: (DL-21-04) 150% Direct Subsidized Loan Limit Electronic Announcement #25: Repeal of the 150% Subsidized Usage Limit

question: Our twins both start college this fall. Does the $65,000 Parent PLUS max get split between them?
reference_answer: No. The $65,000 Parent PLUS aggregate cap applies separately for each dependent student, so each twin has their own limit, and it includes any earlier Parent PLUS borrowed for that child.

sources.title: (LOANS-26-05) One Big Beautiful Bill Act NSLDS Eligibility Processing Updates (Updated May 7, 2026)
Frequently Asked Questions: Loan Limits (FSA, May 20, 2026)

question: Do loans my parents took out for me count toward the $257,500 lifetime borrowing max?
reference_answer: No. The $257,500 lifetime limit covers the Direct and FFEL loans you borrowed as an undergraduate, graduate or professional student, and Parent PLUS loans are excluded from it.

sources.title: (LOANS-26-05) One Big Beautiful Bill Act NSLDS Eligibility Processing Updates (Updated May 7, 2026)

question: If my kid is only half time, does our Parent PLUS loan get reduced too?
reference_answer: No. The new reduction in annual loan limits for students enrolled less than full-time applies to Direct Subsidized and Unsubsidized Loans, but Parent PLUS loans are not subject to it. PLUS is still limited by cost of attendance minus other aid and the Parent PLUS caps.

sources.title: Frequently Asked Questions: Reducing Annual Loan Limits for Less-than-Full-Time Enrollment (FSA)

question: My loan money already posted to my student account and I want to send some back. Is that possible?
reference_answer: Usually, yes. Your school must notify you when loan funds are credited and explain how and by when you can cancel all or part of the loan. Tell your financial aid office within that window and it must return the funds. Within the MPN's time limits, you don't pay interest or the fee on the part you cancel or return.

sources.title: 34 CFR 668.165 Notices and authorizations
Master Promissory Note (MPN): Direct Subsidized Loans and Direct Unsubsidized Loans

question: Can you promise my dad will pass the PLUS credit check if he has no credit history at all?
reference_answer: I can't promise an approval; the Department of Education makes the decision when he applies. Having no credit history is not considered adverse credit, but other factors, such as recent delinquencies, defaults or bankruptcy, can lead to a denial, and he'd still need to meet the other parent eligibility rules.

sources.title: 34 CFR 685.200 Borrower eligibility
